title: Stepwise eastward diversification of the South African velvet worm genus Peripatopsis (Onychophora: Peripatopsidae) evidenced from ultraconserved element data
content:
Abstract
Peripatopsis Pocock, 1894 is one of the best-studied genera of Onychophora, for which extensive anatomical, taxonomic, and evolutionary work exists. The genus has emerged as an example of microspeciation and short-range endemism in South Africa, but evolutionary work has been limited mostly to mitochondrial data. Here we turn to ultraconserved elements to extract phylogenetic (DNA sequence) and population-level (single nucleotide polymorphism [SNP]) data to investigate the evolution and species assignments within this genus. Our results clearly showed a pattern of eastward diversification of Peripatopsis, which may be explained by a combination of abiotic and subsequent floral alterations in South Africa, as major cladogenesis for the genus coincides with the formation of the proto Benguela current and geotectonic uplift, which altered the climatic and orographic landscapes of the Western Cape. At the population level, SNP data illustrate congruence between major geographical clades and putative ancestral groups.
